name: Ally Financial Inc.
moat_justification: Weak-to-moderate franchise: the nation's largest all-digital bank and a leading auto lender (consumer auto originations $13.3B in Q2 2026, +21% YoY; Corporate Finance portfolio $13.7B, +25% YoY) — against a commodity lending product with no structural pricing power, full consumer-credit and rate-cycle exposure, and returns that prove the niche leadership is not translating: GAAP ROE (fundamentals.json, total equity) fell to 7.0% in FY2023, 4.8% in FY2024 and 5.5% in FY2025, below the cost of equity three straight years, with goodwill impairments in all three years ($149M / $118M / $305M) on the exited credit-card and lending adjacencies; core ROTCE of 11.8% in Q2 2026 is a recovery print at a benign point in the credit cycle (retail auto net charge-offs 1.57%), not a through-cycle level. Fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross margin for a bank presentation (both null), so ROE/ROTCE are the return evidence. A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years.

one_liner: Leading digital bank and auto lender in a real ROTCE recovery, moat 4/10 — on the only honest base for a lender (median net income $2.72/sh, not the $13.32/sh OCF artifact) the weighted IRR is 13.54% (IV@15% $32.94 vs $37.68), so it clears 15% only below ~$33; bank-model mismatch, confidence low.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Auto finance leadership at scale — consumer originations $13.3B in Q2 2026 (+21% YoY) on 4.6M applications (+17%); dealer franchise plus insurance (F&I) attached to the same dealer relationships
Largest all-digital US bank — $151,649M of deposits at FY2025 (10-K balance sheet) funding the loan book; 3.6M deposit customers, +7% YoY at Q2 2026
Corporate Finance is a genuine second engine — $13.7B portfolio at Q2 2026, +25% YoY, with a reported 32% ROE in the quarter
Profitability inflecting — core ROTCE 11.8% in Q2 2026 vs 11.0% a year earlier; NIM excluding core OID 3.63%, +18bp YoY; adjusted EPS $1.21, +22% YoY
Credit metrics improving at the print — retail auto net charge-offs 1.57% in Q2 2026, down 18bp YoY and 40bp sequentially
moat_against: Returns below the cost of equity through the recent cycle — GAAP ROE 7.0% / 4.8% / 5.5% in FY2023 / FY2024 / FY2025 (fundamentals.json); the franchise has not earned its capital since FY2022
Commodity product, no structural pricing power — auto loans and deposits are fungible; competition from money-center banks, captive lenders and credit unions sets the price
Consumer credit-cycle and residual-value exposure — provision for credit losses $1,477M in FY2025 ($2,166M in FY2024); operating-lease fleet of $8,772M carries used-vehicle residual risk

Capital-allocation record — goodwill impairments of $149M (FY2023), $118M (FY2024) and $305M (FY2025) on the exited Ally Lending (sold Mar 2024) and Credit Card (sold Apr 1, 2025) businesses; consumer mortgage originations ceased in Q2 2025
Rate sensitivity — NIM depends on deposit repricing and asset yields outside management control; interest on deposits alone was $5,302M in FY2025
